title: One in a million, every day?
hook: A one-in-a-million event should almost never happen. In a big city, how often does it?

knows: '1 in a million' means very rare for one person
multiplying a chance by a number of tries
doesNotKnow: that expected counts scale with the number of chances
that rare events become routine across a population

misconception: A one-in-a-million event essentially never happens.
objective: The learner can explain that the expected number of events is population x chance (8 million x 1 in a million = 8 a day), so an event rare for each person is routine for a city.

claims.text: With 8 million people each facing a 1-in-a-million chance per day, the event happens about 8 times a day on average.
claims.source: Expected count = N x p = 8,000,000 x 0.000001 = 8 (linearity of expectation; expectedPerDay() in src/demos/probability/one-in-a-million-daily/model.ts).

claims.text: The chance that a day in that city passes with no event at all is about 0.03%.
At 10,000 people the same chance gives about 0.01 events a day: roughly one every 100 days.
claims.source: 10,000 x 1e-6 = 0.01 per day; 3.65 expected per 365 days.

claims.text: The stage's year at 8 million had 2,946 events (8.1 a day) and no day without one; at 10,000 people the year had 6 events and 359 empty days.
claims.source: year() in model.ts: seeded Poisson draws with mean N x 1e-6 per day, seed 808 (untuned: the first seed tried). Across seeds 1-500 at 8 million the yearly mean ranged 7.55-8.44 and no year had more than 2 empty days; at 10,000 the yearly total ranged 0-11 (median 3).

claims.text: Daily counts are drawn as Poisson with mean population x chance, which matches the exact binomial count to within rounding at these sizes.
claims.source: Poisson limit of Bin(N, p) for large N and small p; Le Cam's inequality bounds the total variation distance by N p^2 = 8e-6 at 8 million.

claims.text: The model assumes every person faces the same chance, independently, every day.
claims.source: Model assumption, stated on the stage chip and in the reveal.

recall.question: A coincidence has a 1-in-10-million chance per person per year. In a country of 50 million, about how many people experience it each year?
recall.why: Expected count = people x chance = 50,000,000 / 10,000,000 = 5. Rare for each person, routine for a country.
